heads: Modi in Manila for ASEAN and East Asia Summits
Delhi’s air eases to ‘poor’ after rain; ‘very poor’ due back by Tuesday
LeT commander killed in Kulgam; Sensex jumps 512 points

paras.t: Namaskar, and welcome to Pringital News. Credible like print, fast like digital. This is your four-minute bulletin for Monday, the sixteenth of November, twenty twenty-six, from New Delhi.

First, the headlines. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is in Manila for the ASEAN and East Asia Summits. Delhi’s air has eased after rain, but smog is expected back by Tuesday. And a Lashkar commander has been killed in Kulgam.

Prime Minister Modi arrived in the Philippine capital on Monday for the twenty-third India–ASEAN Summit and the twenty-first East Asia Summit, both on Tuesday. He viewed the Laguna Copperplate Inscription, the oldest dated document found in the Philippines, which records ancient links with India. The summits open under strain: ASEAN and China failed to finalise a South China Sea code of conduct, and India restated its support for freedom of navigation.

Delhi’s average air quality index improved to two hundred and thirteen, in the poor band, on Monday morning, after wind and light rain on Sunday. It was three hundred and fifty-three a day earlier. Forecasters expect the air to slip back to very poor on the seventeenth and eighteenth, and stay there for about six days.

In Jammu and Kashmir, security forces killed Lashkar commander Mohammad Latif Bhat and another militant in Kulgam. Bhat was the main suspect in last week’s attack on a C.R.P.F. post. A deep depression in the Bay of Bengal is set to intensify into a cyclonic storm; fishermen have been told to stay away from the Andaman Sea. And India, the United States and eight other countries have signed a declaration to protect artificial-intelligence supply chains.

Prince William and the Princess of Wales have arrived in India for a three-day visit, their first official overseas trip together in four years. They will meet Prime Minister Modi on Wednesday and attend the Earthshot Prize ceremony in Mumbai.

The Sensex rose five hundred and twelve points to close at eighty-two thousand, one hundred and five, and the Nifty ended at twenty-five thousand, two hundred and ninety-one, led by bank and F.M.C.G. shares. The rupee gained thirty-two paise against the dollar. Hindustan Zinc has approved an eighty-thousand-crore-rupee plan to nearly double its metal output.

China has confirmed that Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin will meet in Shenzhen on the nineteenth of November. Russia says it shot down more than one thousand three hundred Ukrainian drones overnight, as a strike halted traffic on the Crimea bridge. And Iran has warned that it may strike first rather than wait for another American attack.

I.P.L. teams announce their retention lists on Tuesday. Rajat Patidar hit thirteen sixes in a knock of one hundred and thirty-five in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy. And Jay Shah has been re-elected unopposed as chairman of the International Cricket Council.

Ramayana has crossed one thousand three hundred and eighty-four crore rupees worldwide in eleven days. And actor Sharad Kapoor, who asked the film industry for help after years of illness, has received support from Salman Khan and a visit from Sonu Sood.

That was your Pringital News bulletin, the day’s important news in four minutes. For the full story, tap the link on your Pringital page. Read it on your phone, share it on WhatsApp, and help save the trees cut for newsprint. Thank you for listening. Namaskar.
